title: Envelope
description: One message on the wire. A reply carries the `id` of the request it answers.

AccessLevel.description: What a workspace's agents may do on one machine, chosen by the machine's owner.

oneOf.description: No agent runs.
Agents ask a person before each change.
Agents change things without asking; destructive operations still ask.

AccountId.description: A person's account on the server, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

AccountSignInFinish.description:
Trades the one-time code sent to `email`, and the challenge its [`SignInStarted`] gave,
for an [`AccountSignedIn`].

AccountSignInStart.description:
Asks the server to send a one-time code to `email`, if that person may sign in. The
answer, a [`SignInStarted`], is the same either way.

AccountSignedIn.description:
The signed-in account. `token`, sent as a bearer token, is only in the answer to an
[`AccountSignInFinish`], for clients that keep no cookie.

oneOf.description: A member's own, under their sign-in.
The workspace's shared agent, under the workspace's own credential.

AgentRef.description: An agent as people know it.

machine.description:
What the machine it runs on is called, which the server stamps from its own record of
the core that sent the status and never takes from the core; left out when not known.

AgentSession.description: An agent's own id for a conversation, a lowercase UUID, which resumes it later.

AnchorChange.description:
What a move did to an anchor's code, each item described in a line such as
`fn a::run  a/src/lib.rs:3`.

App.description: A program, such as `weacon-core`, and the exact build it is.

Asker.description:
Who asked for a command, stamped by the server on what it relays to a machine and never
taken from a client. The core acts only when `account` is its owner's, and records only
`member`.

Author.description: Who made a change, such as one to a task.

oneOf.description: An agent, named by the member it answers to, and by which agent it is when known.

BuildTarget.description: A Rust target a release is built for, such as `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`.

Bytes.description:
Bytes that travel as lowercase hex, at most [`NOISE_MAX`] of them. Its `Debug` shows only
how many, since they are sealed or terminal content.

Capability.description:
A feature a peer supports, such as `chat.send`, named like a [`Code`]. A peer keeps the ones
it doesn't know, so a newer peer's list still parses.

ChallengeId.description:
One sign-in request, which its code and its tries belong to; 1–64 ASCII letters,
digits, `-` or `_`.

oneOf.description:
Starts or queues a turn. Only a chat's first prompt has `repo` and `machine`, one of the
sender's; the server drops `machine` before relaying. `agent` fixes the chat's agent on
its first prompt, Claude when missing; a later prompt naming another agent is refused as
`chat.agent_conflict`, and an agent the core doesn't know as `message.unsupported`.
`task` links a new chat to a task of its workspace; the server relays it with the
task's title as it is then, and a later prompt naming a task with the chat's own, or none.
`pick` names a [`Pick`](crate::Pick) the core keeps, from a local client only; the agent
gets it as quoted page content.
Answers a permission prompt of one of the chat's runs.
Stops the turn that is running.

Holds the chat for a person carrying its session on by hand: while the connection that
sent it is open, no run starts and prompts queue. Sent by a local client under
`chat.hold`, never through the server.
Ends this connection's hold, under `chat.hold`; queued prompts then go on.

ChatAnswer.description:
The core's answer to a [`ChatQuery`], or its word that the client missed events, to a client
that has `chat.events`.

oneOf.description:
The client missed events and its subscription is over: fetch a snapshot, then subscribe
after its `seq`.

The chat as of `seq`: its runs, where in the log the permission prompts still waiting
are, and its latest events, as many as fit one frame. A `window` fetches a prompt that
isn't among them.

ChatCommand.description:
What a person asks of a chat's agent, from a client to a core that offers `chat.send`. The
core answers with receipts under `request`.

by.description: Who asked, when the server relays the command to a machine.

ChatEntry.description: An event and its place in its chat's log: `seq` starts at 1 and grows by one.

oneOf.description:
A person's prompt, accepted under `request`, with the repository, the agent and the
task it named, and a note of the element it carried, if any.
Where a chat command stands; written once per state.
A prompt typed outside Weacon, read from an agent's own session file.

ChatId.description: A chat in a workspace, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

ChatList.description:
A workspace's chats, from the server, to clients that have the capability
`workspace.chats`.

ChatLive.description:
A run's update that a viewer of its chat needs and no one stores: text as it is written, and
the tool a permission prompt names, never its input. From a core to the server, and from the
server to the feeds that follow the chat, each under `chat.live`.

after.description:
The seq of the chat's last event committed before it, in the sender's log: a viewer
that holds a later one shows no text from it.

ChatQuery.description:
A question about a chat's log, from a client to a core that offers `chat.events`. The answer
is a [`ChatAnswer`], or for `subscribe` the [`ChatUpdate`]s themselves.

oneOf.description: Every event after `after`, then each new one as it is committed.

The latest events before `before`: at most `limit`, and fewer when they wouldn't fit
one frame.

ChatState.description: What can still happen to a chat.

oneOf.description: Its owner can prompt it.
Its workspace has no room for more of its events, so it takes no prompts until it has.
Its machine was unpaired, or no longer has its log: it can be read, never prompted.

ChatSummary.description:
A chat in a [`ChatList`]: `machine` is its machine's name and `machine_id` its id, and
`updated_at` is when its latest turn began or ended, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

run.description: What its latest run is doing; left out when it has had none.

task.description: The task it was made for, if any.

ChatTask.description:
The task a chat works on: its id, and its title as the chat's first prompt found it, a
person's words.

ChatUpdate.description:
A committed event of a chat, from the core to a client that subscribed under `chat.events`.
Text deltas are never committed; they arrive only as run updates.

ChatsAnswer.description: The core's answer to a [`ChatsQuery`], under the query's envelope id.

ChatsQuery.description:
A local client asks the core which chats it serves, in every workspace.
Never relayed by the server, which lists a workspace's chats itself.

oneOf.description: Every chat this core has run or queued a prompt for, newest first.

ClientLog.description:
A log record from a client that has no log of its own, such as the web app: an event name
and typed ids, sent only to a peer that offers `log.forward`. The receiver logs only events
it knows, so no other text reaches its log.

Code.description:
A dotted code such as `store.full`: two or more lowercase words joined by dots. It names
errors, and capabilities too.

Commit.description: A full git commit id: 40 lowercase hex digits. Unlike a doc's `CommitId`, not 64.

CommitId.description: A git commit, as 40 or 64 lowercase hex digits.

DiffAnswer.description: From the core to a client that has `diff.view`, in answer to a [`DiffQuery`].

oneOf.description:
One of the `files` changed files, which arrive one answer each, in order; `files` is at
least 1 and the same in every answer to one query.
Nothing changed.
No hunks when only the file's mode changed.
The file's changes wouldn't fit one frame.

path.description: Where the file is now, or was when it was removed, relative to the worktree.

DiffLine.description: One line without its `\n`, so a `\r` before it stays in `text`.

no_newline.description: The file's last line, when it has no `\n`.

DiffQuery.description:
From a client to a core that offers `diff.view`. Each answer is a [`DiffAnswer`] that echoes
`request`.

by.description:
Who asked, stamped by the server when it relays the query to a machine; a client's own
value is overwritten.

oneOf.description: Every file the chat's agents changed in its worktree.

DocAnchors.description: A pin for each anchor a doc links to, all computed at `commit`.

repo.description:
The workspace's repository the pins are of; when absent, any repository's move may
check them.

DocContent.description:
What one revision of a doc says: its title, its Markdown, and the anchors it links to,
unless it links to none.

DocHistory.description: A doc's revisions, newest first, from the server.

DocId.description: A doc in a workspace, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

DocList.description: A workspace's docs, from the server.

DocPin.description:
An anchor a doc links to, with the fingerprint the code had at the revision's commit:
`sym:weacon_protocol::frame::encode_line#0123456789abcdef`, in printable ASCII. The core
computes both; the server only checks their shape.

DocRecord.description:
A doc at one revision; `version` rises with each revision. The server sends it to clients
that have the capability `workspace.docs`.

DocRevise.description:
Asks the server for a new revision of a doc that the client read at `version`; the server
refuses when the doc has changed since. The answer is its [`DocRecord`].

DocRevision.description:
Who made one revision of a doc, who accepted it, and when, in seconds since the Unix
epoch.

DocSummary.description: A doc in a [`DocList`], without its body.

DownloadUrl.description:
An `https://` address of printable ASCII, at most 2,048 bytes, with a plain host name and
optionally a port: no user name or password.

ErrorBody.description: Why a request failed, in an error message or an HTTP error answer.

retryable.description: Whether the same request can succeed if sent again later.

Hello.description: The first message on every connection, from the side that connects.

Hunk.description:
A run of changed lines and their context. Lines count from 1; the start of a side with no
lines, as the old side of an added file, is 0.

oneOf.description:
Given only while no chat is busy. From then on no turn starts and no chat can be held
until `failed`, until the asker hangs up, or until the leave runs out.

The new build is in place and the daemon is about to be restarted; turns stay paused,
even once the asker hangs up, until the leave runs out again. Refused once the leave has
run out, and the asker then puts the old build back.
The install failed and the build before it is back; turns go on.

InstallCommand.description:
From `weacon update` to its own core's daemon that offers `update.leave`, over the daemon's
local socket: leave to install a build that restarts the daemon, then how the install went.
The daemon answers each with a [`crate::Receipt`] that echoes `request`, or with the error
`update.chat_busy` when it refuses leave, or `update.no_leave` for a report without leave.

Invitation.description:
A live invitation as the workspace's owner sees it: its address, and when it ends, in seconds
since the Unix epoch.

InvitationOffer.description:
A live invitation as the person it is addressed to sees it once signed in, which they take up
with `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace}/accept`.

oneOf.description: Very noisy.
Developer detail.
Lifecycle.
Failed and handled.
A person needs to look.
About to exit.

LocalChat.description:
A chat a core serves: `title` is its first prompt's first line, as the server titles it, and
`updated_at` is when its latest turn began or ended, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

run.description: What its latest run is doing; left out when it has had none.

LogEvent.description:
What happened, such as `run started`: one to four words of lowercase letters or `_`, one
space apart, at most 40 bytes; no digits, so ids and secrets can't be spelt in it.

MachineId.description: A machine paired with an account, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

MachineKey.description:
A machine's public X25519 key, the static key of its sealed channels, as 64 lowercase hex
digits. A browser pins it when the person confirms the pairing.

MachineList.description: The machines paired with the signed-in account.

MachineName.description:
What a machine is called: 1–64 characters, none of them control or bidirectional
formatting characters, so it shows the same wherever it is shown.

MachineOs.description: The operating system a machine runs.

MachineSettings.description: What a machine keeps for one workspace, and whether it sends error reports.

reports.description: The owner's answer to error reports; absent until they give one, when none are sent.

sign_ins.description: Each agent the core runs, signed in or not with the workspace's own config folder.

team.description: Whether other people are in the workspace.

oneOf.description: Whether the machine sends error reports; for the whole machine, not one workspace.

What `workspace`'s agents may do on the machine, and whether other people are in it;
`team` is kept as it was when left out.

MachineSettingsAnswer.description:
From the core to a client that has `machine.settings`, in answer to a
[`MachineSettingsQuery`] or a [`MachineSettingsCommand`].

oneOf.description:
The ids of the workspace's repositories, sorted. Where each is on the machine is never
said: everyone who may ask would see it.

MachineSettingsCommand.description:
From the owner of `machine` to its core, which offers `machine.settings`: changes what the
machine keeps for `workspace`. The server relays it only from the machine's owner, and the
core acts only when `by` is its owner; the answer is a [`MachineSettingsAnswer`] that echoes
`request` and holds the settings after the change.

by.description: Who asked, when the server relays the message to a machine.

MachineSettingsQuery.description:
From the owner of `machine` to its core, which offers `machine.settings`: what the machine
keeps for `workspace`. The server relays it only from the machine's owner, and the core
answers only when `by` is its owner; the answer is a [`MachineSettingsAnswer`] that echoes
`request`.

by.description: Who asked, when the server relays the message to a machine.

oneOf.description: The settings as they are now.

The repositories the owner registered for the workspace, of a core that offers
`repo.list`; an older core answers `request.unknown`.

MachineSummary.description:
A machine paired with the signed-in account, at `paired_at`, in seconds since the Unix
epoch.

connected.description: Whether its core is connected now.

core.description: The core's build when it last connected; none until it has.

missing.description:
What the server offers cores that this one didn't offer back when it last connected:
it is older than the server supports, and those features don't reach it.

MapAnswer.description: The core's answer to a [`MapQuery`], under its envelope id.

text.description: None when the core has no map to give for that token and folder.

MapArgs.description:
From a run's agent, under `McpCall::Map` or `McpCall::Hotspots`, or its hook, under
`MapQueryKind::Map`: how much of the map it wants.

budget.description: The most bytes the answer may hold; the core clamps it to its own bounds.

MapQuery.description:
From a hook that an agent the core started runs, to that core over its socket, under
`map.read`: the code map of `folder`, in the workspace of the run whose MCP token it holds.

token.description: The run's token for the core's MCP.

oneOf.description: Where to begin reading the folder's code, as the MCP's `map` tool answers.

What a session starts with: the flows
pinned by the docs that best match the title of the task of the run's chat, then the
folder's map, both within `budget`; the map alone for a chat without a task.

Mark.description:
The part of a [`Snippet`] from `start` up to `end`, counted in UTF-16 code units as a
browser counts a string.

oneOf.description:
Invites `email` for seven days; only the owner may. The answer is the same whether or not
the address has an account.
Ends the live invitation to `email`; only the owner may.
Ends a member's membership; only the owner may.
Ends the asker's own membership; the owner can't.

MemberCommand.description:
Asks the server, as `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace}/members`, to change who is in the
workspace.

MemberId.description: A member of a workspace, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

MemberList.description:
A workspace's members, past ones included, in the order they were added, from the server to
clients that have the capability `workspace.members`. Only its owner gets the live
invitations.

MemberSummary.description:
A member as the workspace's other members see them, under the name the server shows for
them.

role.description: Their role; left out for a past member.

MergeHunk.description:
A run of a doc's body in a [`ProposalOutcome::DocConflict`]; the hunks in order are the
whole body.

oneOf.description: Lines the merge settled: the same on both sides, or changed on one only.
Lines the doc and the proposal both changed since `base`, each in its own way.

Outcome.description:
Where an accepted command stands. It ends `completed`, `interrupted`, `failed` or `unknown`.
`unknown` means it may or may not have run, as when a restart cut it off; the client must not
send it again under a new id.

OutsideSession.description:
A session a person ran with their own agent outside Weacon, last changed at `modified_at`,
in seconds since the Unix epoch.

folder.description: The folder it ran in, when its file names one.

PairClaim.description:
From the core that started `pairing`: whether the person has confirmed it yet. The answer
is a [`PairClaimed`].

oneOf.description: Not confirmed yet: claim again later.

Paired with `owner`'s account. The core proves itself with `token`, sent as a bearer
token, which every claim with the pairing's secret returns until the pairing expires or
the machine is unpaired.

PairConfirm.description:
From the web app, signed in: pairs the machine waiting under `code` with the signed-in
account. The answer is its [`MachineSummary`].

PairLookup.description:
From the web app, signed in: the machine waiting under `code`. The answer is a
[`PairPending`].

PairPending.description: A machine waiting to be paired, for the person to check against what its terminal shows.

PairStart.description:
From a core to the server, unauthenticated: starts pairing the machine. The answer is a
[`PairStarted`]; the server refuses an `os` it doesn't know.

PairStarted.description:
The answer to a [`PairStart`]: the single-use `code` the person enters in the web app, and
the `secret` only the core that started may claim the machine with, until `expires_at`, in
seconds since the Unix epoch.

PairingId.description:
One pairing of a machine, from its start to its claim; 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-`
or `_`.

Pick.description:
An element someone picked in Chrome, from the extension to a core that offers `element.pick`,
which keeps it on the machine for a prompt that names its `request`. The
sender cuts the HTML short and shrinks the screenshot so the message fits in one frame.
Everything in it comes from the page, so it is untrusted.

component.description: The name of the component that rendered the element, where the page's framework says.

screenshot_png.description:
What the element looked like: a PNG, base64-encoded. None when the page couldn't be
captured.

selector.description: A CSS selector that finds the element on the page.

source.description: The source file of that component, where the framework says, as the page names it.

PickNote.description:
What a chat's log keeps of a pick a prompt carried: the page's address without its query,
fragment or sign-in, its title and the element's selector, never its HTML or screenshot.

PinnedDoc.description: A doc's anchors at its revision `version`.

ProposalAbout.description: The doc or task a proposal is about; a new one has the id it gets once accepted.

oneOf.description:
Proposes `change`, made by an agent of `agent`'s kind, which the server can't check. An
edit takes the place of the same machine's open edit of the same doc or task.
Withdraws one of the same machine's open proposals.

Proposes `proposals` together, as the core's own for its owner rather than an agent's:
what one move of the code did to one doc's anchors. All are stored, or none is.

ProposalAnswer.description: The server's answer to a [`ProposalQuery`], under its `request`.

oneOf.description: Docs that pin code, by id; `more` when others follow the last.

ProposalChange.description: What a proposal would change once a person accepts it.

oneOf.description: The doc's whole new content, written from its revision `base`.
At least one edit to the task, made from its version `base`.
A doc to make, at its first revision.
A task to do, placed last.

The code that some of the doc's anchors pin changed or went, as of its revision `base`,
so its text may need an update; accepting it changes nothing but says a person saw it.

ProposalCommand.description:
What an agent asks the server for, from a core to a server that offers
`workspace.proposals`, for one of its owner's agents. The server answers with receipts under
`request`, and names the owner and machine itself.

ProposalDecision.description:
A member's decision on an open proposal, from a client to the server. The answer is a
[`ProposalOutcome`].

ProposalId.description:
A proposal in a workspace, chosen by the core that proposes it and kept across
reconnects: sending it again with the same change is the same proposal, while the same
id with another change, or from another machine, is refused with `proposal.conflict`.
1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

ProposalList.description: A workspace's proposals, newest first, from the server.

ProposalOutcome.description:
What a [`ProposalDecision`] came to. A conflict changes nothing: the proposal stays open,
and the person edits the doc or task themselves, then rejects it.

oneOf.description: The doc or task is now at `version`.

The doc changed since the proposal's base where the proposal changed it too: in its
body, as `hunks` show, its title, or the anchors it links to.
The proposal's `edits` that change what changed in the task since the proposal's base.

ProposalQuery.description:
What a core asks a server that offers `workspace.proposals` about its owner's workspace,
to propose what a move of the code did to its docs. The answer is a [`ProposalAnswer`].

oneOf.description: The docs that pin code, by id, from the first after `after`.
One doc as it is now, or as the core's own open re-anchor of its revision would make it.

ProposalRecord.description:
A proposal, from the server to clients that have the capability `workspace.proposals`, at
`at` seconds since the Unix epoch. Its author's machine is a name, never an id, and only an
open proposal still holds its `change`.

oneOf.description: Accepted by `by`, which made the doc or task `version`.

Receipt.description: The core's or server's word on a command, sent when it accepts it and again when it ends.

ReleaseBuild.description: One target's binary in a release.

ReleaseManifest.description: A release, as its signed manifest describes it; a core reads it to update itself.

builds.description: At most one for each target.

published_at.description:
When the release was signed, in seconds since the Unix epoch, so a core can tell a
manifest that is being held back from the newest one.

ReleaseVersion.description: A release's `major.minor.patch`, ordered by its numbers.

RepoId.description:
A git repository the owner registered for a workspace on their machine, 1–64 ASCII
letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

RequestId.description:
A command's id, chosen by the client and kept across reconnects and retries. Sending the
same id again returns the first receipt instead of repeating the work; the same id with
different content is refused with the error `request.conflict`.

RunEvent.description: What an agent's run reports, in order. Each turn ends with `finished`.

oneOf.description: The agent's conversation, to resume it later.
More of the text block being written; the [`RunEvent::Text`] that follows replaces it.
The agent asks to use a tool and waits for a [`PermissionAnswer`].
The agent no longer waits for the answer to `prompt`.
A person answered a waiting prompt; committed before the agent is told.
Ends the turn and withdraws any prompt still waiting.

RunId.description:
The core's id for one run of an agent process, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.
Prompts carry it, so an answer only ever reaches the run that asked.

oneOf.description: The agent process is starting.
On a turn.
On a turn, waiting for a person to answer a permission prompt.
Between turns, with its process alive.
Its process was stopped; the next prompt resumes the same agent session in a new run.
Over for good.

RunStatus.description: Where a run stands, as its chat's log records it.

agent.description: Who runs it; left out when not known.

RunUpdate.description:
One event of the run `run`, in the order the run reported it, from the core to clients that
have `run.stream`.

SearchAnswer.description:
The server's answer to a [`SearchQuery`]: matches in the title first, then the most
recently changed.

SearchHit.description: One thing a [`SearchQuery`] found, with its title and where it matched.

oneOf.description:
A chat, by its title or by one of the messages its log keeps: a person's prompt or an
agent's text. `seq` is that message's place in the log.

SearchQuery.description:
Asks the server, under the capability `workspace.search`, for the tasks, docs and chats in
the workspace that hold every word of `text`, at most 8 words of at most 64 characters, in
256 bytes. Words of three or more characters match whatever their case and accents; shorter
ones match as typed, ignoring only ASCII case, and text without a longer word finds nothing.
`limit` is 20 without one, and at most 50.

SessionsAnswer.description:
The core's answer to a [`SessionsQuery`] under the same `request`, to a client that has
`sessions.read`.

oneOf.description:
Events in the file's order, each `seq` its place there, the agent's as runs whose id is
the session's; with `more`, ask again after the last `seq`.
No such session in the person's own config folders.

SessionsQuery.description:
A person asks their own machine about the agent sessions they ran outside Weacon, from a
client to a core that offers `sessions.read`. No workspace holds these sessions.

by.description:
The account that asked, when the server relays the message to a machine; the core
answers only its owner.

oneOf.description: The sessions in the person's own config folders, newest first.
The session's events after `after`, as many as fit one frame.

Sha256.description: A SHA-256 digest: 64 lowercase hex digits. Not the `sha2::Sha256` hasher.

SignInFinish.description:
Trades the one-time code sent to `email` for a [`SignedIn`]. `challenge` is the one its
[`SignInStarted`] gave; a server that hands out challenges refuses a finish without one.

SignInStart.description:
Sign-in to one workspace, which [`AccountSignInStart`] replaces: asks the server to send a
one-time code to `email`, if it is a member of `workspace`. The answer, a [`SignInStarted`],
is the same either way.

SignInStarted.description:
The answer to a [`SignInStart`], for members and strangers alike: the challenge to finish
it with.

SignInState.description: Only whether an agent is signed in: never its credentials.

oneOf.description: The vendor's tool didn't say.

SignedIn.description: A signed-in member and the session token that proves it, sent as a bearer token.

Snippet.description: Plain text from around a match, and the parts of it that matched.

StaleAnchor.description: An anchor of a doc whose code a move changed.

pin.description: The pin as the doc has it.

Symbol.description: An item of a repository's code: where it is, never what it holds.

line.description: The line it begins at, counting from 1.

name.description: Its path in the code, such as `weacon_protocol::message::Envelope`.

path.description: Its file, from the repository's root, joined with `/`.

SymbolsAnswer.description:
The core's answer to a [`SymbolsQuery`] under the same `request`, to a client that has
`symbols.search`.

oneOf.description: The best of each repository in turn; `more` when some were left out.

SymbolsQuery.description:
A person asks their own machine for the items of the code in the repositories it has for a
workspace, from a client to a core that offers `symbols.search`. Neither the query nor its
answer is stored.

by.description:
Who asked, when the server relays the message to a machine; the core answers only its
owner.

oneOf.description:
The items whose path, or a contract they declare, holds every word, or a word's start,
best first.

TaskChange.description:
Asks the server to change a task that the client read at `version`; the server refuses
when the task has changed since. The answer is its [`TaskRecord`].

TaskCreate.description:
Asks the server for a new task, placed in front of `before`, or last without one. The
answer is its [`TaskRecord`].

TaskEditBody.description: One edit to a task, inside a [`TaskChange`].

oneOf.description: Places the task in front of `before`, or last without one.

TaskId.description: A task in a workspace, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

TaskList.description: A workspace's tasks in their order, from the server.

TaskRecord.description:
A task as it travels: `order` is its order key and `version` rises with each change. The
server sends it to clients that have the capability `workspace.tasks`.

TaskStatus.description: How far along a task is.

oneOf.description:
Runs `agent`'s login, with the first handshake message, whose payload is a
[`TerminalInput::Resize`].
A sealed [`TerminalInput`].
Ends the login, if it still runs.

TerminalCommand.description:
A sign-in terminal's sealed input, from the owner of `machine`'s browser to its core, which
offers `terminal.sign_in`. The server relays it only when it offers `terminal.relay`, and
only from the machine's owner, and the core acts only when `by` is its owner and refuses a
terminal id it has already seen.

by.description: Who asked, when the server relays the message to a machine.

oneOf.description: The second handshake message, with an empty payload.
A sealed [`TerminalOutput`].
The terminal is gone; nothing more comes. `code` says why, unless it ended as asked.

TerminalId.description:
One sign-in terminal, chosen by the browser that opens it; 1–64 ASCII letters, digits,
`-` or `_`.

TerminalInput.description: From the browser to the core, only inside the seal.

oneOf.description: What the person typed or pasted.
The terminal's size in characters.

TerminalOutput.description: From the core to the browser, only inside the seal.

oneOf.description: What the login printed.
The login ended, and then the vendor's status command said this.

TerminalUpdate.description:
A sign-in terminal's sealed output, from a core that offers `terminal.sign_in`, through the
server, to the browser that opened `terminal`.

UpdateSchedule.description: When a core looks for a release, chosen by its owner. Only `off` keeps it from ever asking.

oneOf.description: Look once a day and say when one is out; install only when asked.
Look once a day and install what's out.
Look once a week and install what's out.

Welcome.description: The answer to a [`Hello`] that speaks the same protocol.

oneOf.description: A member opened the workspace for the first time.

Someone was invited, joined, left or was removed, or an invitation ended; clients read
the members again.

A task was made, at version 1, or changed. Only for clients that have the capability
`workspace.tasks`, which read the tasks again to see what it now is.

A doc was made, at version 1, or revised. Only for clients that have the capability
`workspace.docs`, which read the doc again to see what it now says.

A chat was made, or its title, state, latest turn or latest run changed. Only for clients
that have the capability `workspace.chats`, which read the chats again.

A proposal was made or its state changed. Only for clients that have the capability
`workspace.proposals`, which read the proposals again.

WorkspaceCreate.description:
Asks the server for a new workspace, which the asker owns. The answer is its
[`WorkspaceSummary`].

WorkspaceId.description: A workspace on the server, 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-` or `_`.

WorkspaceList.description: The workspaces the signed-in account is a member of, and the live invitations to its address.

WorkspaceRole.description: What a member may do in a workspace.

oneOf.description: Made the workspace; there is one.
Was added to it.

WorkspaceSummary.description: A workspace as one of its members sees it, with their `role` in it.

member.description: The signed-in person's own member in this workspace, sent by the server.

WorkspaceUpdate.description:
One change to `workspace`, from the server to clients that have `workspace.feed`. `seq` grows
strictly within a workspace, and a feed opened with `since=N` sends every change after `N`.

oneOf.description: Moves the worktree to the Trash; its branch stays.
Brings the worktree back from the Trash to where it was.
Pushes the chat's branch and opens a draft pull request from it.

Opens a terminal at the chat's worktree, or its working folder without one, on the core's
machine; only its owner may ask, of a core that offers `worktree.open_terminal`.

WorktreeAnswer.description:
From the core to a client that has `worktree.manage`, in answer to a [`WorktreeQuery`] or a
[`WorktreeCommand`].

oneOf.description:
Where the worktree stands, in the Trash or not. A chat with no worktree yet gets the
error `worktree.none`.
The branch was pushed and a draft pull request opened at `url`.

The branch was pushed, but no pull request could be opened from here; `url` is the
page where the person can open one.
A terminal was opened on the core's machine.

WorktreeCommand.description:
From a client to a core that offers `worktree.manage`: what a person asks of a chat's
worktree. The core acts only for someone who may act on the chat, and a client asks the
person before `remove`, whatever the access level. The answer is a [`WorktreeAnswer`] that
echoes `request`: the worktree's state after `remove` or `restore`, which a repeated one
answers too.

by.description: Who asked, when the server relays the command to a machine.

WorktreeQuery.description:
From a client to a core that offers `worktree.manage`: a question about a chat's worktree.
The answer is a [`WorktreeAnswer`] that echoes `request`.

by.description: Who asked, when the server relays the query to a machine.

oneOf.description: Whether the worktree is in the Trash, and what removing it would set aside.
